storage: Derivative(-phi(x, y, z, t)*rho_v(x, y, z, t) + rho_v(x, y, z, t), t)

-Derivative(D(phi(x, y, z, t), T(x, y, z, t))*Derivative(rho_v(x, y, z, t), y), y)

phase change: Derivative(phi(x, y, z, t)*rho_i(T(x, y, z, t)), t)

storage: (1 - phi(x, y, z, t))*Derivative(rho_v(x, y, z, t), t)

agent's symbols.name: rho_i(T)
agent's symbols.meaning: density of ice (mass of ice per unit volume of ice)

agent's symbols.name: D(phi, T)
agent's symbols.meaning: effective diffusivity of water vapor through the pore gas, per unit total cross-section (includes the gas fraction, tortuosity and any Knudsen correction; tends to 0 in the ice)

agent's symbols.name: m_w
agent's symbols.meaning: total water mass (ice plus vapor) per unit total volume

agent's symbols.name: j_v
agent's symbols.meaning: mass flux of water vapor per unit total area

agent's symbols.name: Omega
agent's symbols.meaning: arbitrary fixed control volume with boundary $\partial\Omega$ and outward unit normal $\mathbf{n}$

agent's symbols.name: sigma
agent's symbols.meaning: mass rate of sublimation (ice to vapor) per unit total volume

agent left out.effect: Advection of vapor by bulk gas flow, including Stefan flow caused by sublimation
agent left out.why: Vapor is a trace species or the gas is rarefied; the Stefan velocity is about $\sigma/\rho_{gas}$ and gives a Peclet number $vL/D\ll 1$ at pore scale ($L\sim10^{-5}$ m).
The Soret coefficient for water in air is about $10^{-3}$ K$^{-1}$ or smaller, so it is small next to the Fickian flux from the much steeper dependence of saturation density on $T$.

agent left out.effect: Surface diffusion of adsorbed water on grains and ice
agent left out.why: Adsorbed mass on the grains is not part of the model; its flux is small next to gas-phase transport for pore sizes much larger than the adsorbed layer.

agent left out.effect: Motion and creep of the ice
agent left out.why: Ice creep velocities at 200 K are many orders of magnitude slower than sublimation fronts.
Kept in the result through $\rho_i(T)$; ice thermal expansion is about $1.5\times10^{-4}$ K$^{-1}$, so setting $\rho_i$ constant changes the result by under 0.1% per 10 K if a later task wants it.

agent left out.effect: Water bound in or adsorbed on regolith grains
agent left out.why: Outside the ice-gas pore model by the statement.
